title: SwiftUI: Lists, Navigation and Tabs
theory: In SwiftUI, 'List' displays scrollable rows and 'ForEach' generates views from a collection; both must identify each element, either through 'Identifiable' conformance (an 'id' property) or through the 'id:' parameter with a key path such as '\.self'. 'Section' groups rows under a header, 'swipeActions' adds buttons when a row is swiped, and 'onDelete' and 'onMove' (available on dynamic views such as 'ForEach', not on static rows) enable deleting and reordering. Modern navigation uses 'NavigationStack': you declare 'NavigationLink(value:)' with a 'Hashable' value and, in a single place, 'navigationDestination(for:)' says which view to show for that type. To navigate from code, keep a 'NavigationPath' in '@State', pass it as 'NavigationStack(path:)', and use 'append' to push and 'removeLast' to go back. The title and toolbar are set on the content view with 'navigationTitle' and 'toolbar', never on the NavigationStack itself. 'TabView' with 'Tab' creates tabs, 'NavigationSplitView' builds two- or three-column layouts (which collapse into a stack on iPhone), 'searchable' adds a search field bound to a text (you filter the data yourself) and 'refreshable' enables pull to refresh with an 'async' closure. Common mistakes: forgetting the 'navigationDestination' that matches the value type, using 'ForEach(0..<array.count)' with mutable data, and expecting 'searchable' to filter on its own. In the Certiport exam and the Develop in Swift curriculum, building lists and navigation hierarchies is the foundation of almost every app.
corporateCase: An order management app shows a list of orders grouped into sections by status, with 'swipeActions' to archive and 'searchable' to find customers. Tapping an order pushes the detail through 'NavigationLink(value:)', and a 'NavigationPath' lets the user return to the root after finishing the service.
gameCase: In a game, the main menu is a 'TabView' with Shop, Inventory and Ranking tabs. The inventory uses 'NavigationSplitView' on iPad, with the item list on the left and the selected item detail on the right, and 'refreshable' reloads the online ranking.

quiz.question: What does List(items) { ... } require when you do not pass 'id:'?
options: That the elements be Identifiable (or that the id be given explicitly)
That the list be inside a NavigationStack
quiz.explanation: To know which row changed, was inserted or removed, SwiftUI needs a stable identity. 'Identifiable' types provide 'id'; otherwise use 'id: \.property'.

quiz.question: Where can 'onDelete(perform:)' be applied to enable swipe-to-delete?
options: On a static List with hand-written rows
On the ForEach that generates the rows
On any Text inside the List
quiz.explanation: 'onDelete' and 'onMove' belong to dynamic views such as 'ForEach'. The closure receives an 'IndexSet' with the positions to remove from your array.

quiz.question: You use NavigationLink(value: task) but no screen opens when tapped. What is the most likely cause?
options: A 'navigationDestination(for: Tarefa.self)' is missing inside the NavigationStack
The value must be a String
NavigationLink does not work inside a List
quiz.explanation: With value-based links, the NavigationStack looks for a destination registered for the value's type. Without 'navigationDestination(for:)' for 'Tarefa', nothing is pushed.

quiz.question: How do you go back to the root screen from code using 'var path: NavigationPath'?
quiz.explanation: 'NavigationPath' is a collection of pushed values. Removing every item with 'removeLast(path.count)' returns to the start; 'dismiss' only closes the current screen.

quiz.question: Where is 'navigationTitle' correctly applied?
options: On the content view inside the NavigationStack
On the NavigationStack, after the braces
quiz.explanation: The title belongs to the screen (the content view) shown inside the stack, because each pushed screen can have its own title. Applying it to the NavigationStack itself does not give the expected result.

quiz.question: Which code creates a tab in modern SwiftUI (iOS 18+)?
options: Tab("Home", systemImage: "house") { HomeView() } inside a TabView
quiz.explanation: 'Tab(_:systemImage:content:)' declares title, icon and content. The earlier form, '.tabItem { }' applied to each view, remains valid in older versions.

quiz.question: What does the 'refreshable' modifier receive?
options: An asynchronous closure; the loading indicator stays until it finishes
A synchronous closure run on every frame
A number of seconds between refreshes
quiz.explanation: 'refreshable { await reload() }' enables the pull-to-refresh gesture. Because the closure is 'async', SwiftUI keeps the spinner until it completes.

quiz.question: What is wrong with 'ForEach(0..<tasks.count) { i in ... }' when tasks can be added and removed?
options: The range is not constant and can produce invalid indices when the array changes; prefer 'ForEach(tasks)' with Identifiable
Nothing, it is the recommended form
quiz.explanation: A ForEach over a variable range depends on indices that stop existing when the array shrinks, causing warnings or crashes. Use the collection itself with a stable identity.

extraQuiz.question: What is 'NavigationSplitView' for?
options: Opening two modal screens at once
Building sidebar, content and detail layouts that collapse into a stack on compact screens
extraQuiz.explanation: It is the basis of Mail- and Notes-style apps: two or three columns on iPad and Mac, and stack navigation on iPhone.

extraQuiz.question: What happens when you use 'searchable(text: $query)' on a List?
options: SwiftUI shows the field, but you filter the data yourself based on 'query'
The list is filtered automatically by the row texts
The field only appears on macOS
extraQuiz.explanation: 'searchable' only provides the field and the text binding. The filtering logic (for example a computed property) is your code's responsibility.

extraQuiz.question: What is the role of 'Section' in a List?
options: Grouping rows with an optional header and footer
extraQuiz.explanation: 'Section("Pending") { ForEach(...) }' organizes rows into groups, which is common in Settings and agenda screens.

extraQuiz.question: What is needed for 'onMove' to reorder rows?
options: An edit mode (for example EditButton) and moving the data with 'move(fromOffsets:toOffset:)'
extraQuiz.explanation: The 'onMove' closure receives an 'IndexSet' and a destination, and you must update the array, usually with 'array.move(fromOffsets:toOffset:)'. Edit mode shows the drag handles.

extraQuiz.question: How does 'NavigationPath' differ from a typed array like '[Tarefa]' in 'NavigationStack(path:)'?
options: 'NavigationPath' accepts Hashable values of different types, while the array holds a single type
extraQuiz.explanation: With 'NavigationPath' you push mixed types (Tarefa, Cliente...), each with its own 'navigationDestination'. A typed array fits when the whole stack has one type.

extraQuiz.question: What is the advantage of 'NavigationLink(value:)' over 'NavigationLink(destination:)'?
options: The destination is decoupled and declared once, and the stack can be controlled from code
extraQuiz.explanation: With values, the destination is registered centrally and created only when needed, and the same value can be pushed from code through 'NavigationPath'.

title: SwiftUI: Forms and Input Controls
theory: 'Form' is a container that groups input controls and adapts to the platform style (on iOS, a grouped list). Controls connect to state through a Binding, obtained with the '$' prefix on a '@State' property: 'TextField' and 'SecureField' edit a String, 'TextEditor' edits multi-line text, 'Toggle(isOn:)' edits a Bool, 'Slider' and 'Stepper' edit numbers (Slider uses Double) and 'DatePicker' edits a Date. 'Picker' ties the selection to the 'tag' of each option, and the tag type must be exactly the selection type, including Optional. Styles such as '.menu', '.segmented', '.wheel' and '.navigationLink' change the appearance. 'Button' accepts a 'role' such as '.destructive' or '.cancel', which gives semantic and visual meaning, and 'Menu' groups actions. For the keyboard, 'keyboardType', 'textContentType', 'submitLabel' and 'onSubmit' improve typing, and '@FocusState' with 'focused(_:equals:)' controls which field is active. Validation is usually done with computed properties that feed 'disabled()' on the submit button. 'Link' opens a URL and 'ShareLink' opens the share sheet. For accessibility, the control's title becomes the VoiceOver label; icon-only controls need 'accessibilityLabel'.
corporateCase: A banking app has a sign-up form with an email TextField (email keyboard and 'submitLabel(.next)'), a password SecureField and a 'Create account' button that stays 'disabled' until the email and password are valid. '@FocusState' moves the cursor to the next field when the user taps Return.
gameCase: On a game's settings screen, a 'Slider' adjusts the volume, a 'Toggle' turns vibration on, a segmented 'Picker' chooses the difficulty and a 'Stepper' sets the number of players. A 'ShareLink' lets players share the room code with friends.

quiz.question: What is the role of 'Form' in SwiftUI?
options: Grouping input controls, adopting the platform's form style
quiz.explanation: 'Form' only organizes and styles controls (on iOS, a grouped list). Validation and submission are your own logic.

quiz.question: What does '$text' mean when passed to a TextField?
options: A Binding<String> that lets the field read and write the state
quiz.explanation: The '$' prefix accesses the 'projectedValue' of '@State', a Binding. It gives the control read and write access to the state.

quiz.question: You have '@State var cor: Cor? = nil' and options with '.tag(Cor.azul)'. The selection never shows. Why?
options: The tag is Cor but the selection is Cor?; the types do not match. Use '.tag(Cor?.some(.azul))'
quiz.explanation: Picker compares the tag with the selection value, type for type. With an optional selection, the tags must be optional too.

quiz.question: What is '@FocusState' for?
options: Reading and setting which text field has focus, together with 'focused(_:equals:)'
quiz.explanation: With an enum of fields and '.focused($campo, equals: .email)' you move focus from code, for example in 'onSubmit'.

quiz.question: Which modifier changes the text of the keyboard's Return key?
quiz.explanation: 'submitLabel(.next)', '.done', '.search' and so on set the key label; 'onSubmit' runs the action when it is tapped.

quiz.question: What does the '.destructive' role do on a Button?
options: Semantically marks a destructive action, usually highlighted in red; the action itself is still your code
quiz.explanation: The role conveys meaning to the system and to accessibility, but it does not run anything by itself.

quiz.question: What is the best way to prevent submitting a form with an empty email?
options: '.disabled(email.isEmpty)' on the button, computed from state
quiz.explanation: 'disabled' takes a condition derived from state, updated automatically, and also tells accessibility that the button is unavailable.

quiz.question: Why does 'Slider(value: $volume, in: 0...10)' not compile when 'volume' is '@State var volume = 5'?
options: The state must be a String
Inference creates an Int, but Slider needs a floating-point value such as Double
quiz.explanation: '5' becomes Int by default. Declare 'var volume: Double = 5' (or '5.0') so the Binding has the expected type.

extraQuiz.question: What is the main difference between 'TextEditor' and 'TextField'?
options: TextEditor edits multi-line text but has no built-in placeholder
TextField does not use a Binding
extraQuiz.explanation: 'TextEditor' is the option for long text. For a growing field, 'TextField' with 'axis: .vertical' is also possible.

extraQuiz.question: Which parameter limits the DatePicker to choosing only the date, without the time?
extraQuiz.explanation: 'displayedComponents' accepts '.date', '.hourAndMinute' or both. The 'in:' parameter restricts the allowed range.

extraQuiz.question: Which Picker style shows a few options side by side in a segmented control?
extraQuiz.explanation: '.pickerStyle(.segmented)' is ideal for 2 to 4 short options. In a Form, the default style on iOS is navigationLink (pushes a selection screen); outside a Form, the default is the menu.

extraQuiz.question: What is the difference between 'Link' and 'ShareLink'?
options: Link opens a URL; ShareLink opens the system share sheet
extraQuiz.explanation: 'Link("Site", destination: url)' navigates to the URL; 'ShareLink(item: url)' presents the share sheet to send the content.

extraQuiz.question: How does Toggle('Notifications', isOn: $on) behave with VoiceOver?
options: The control's title is used as the label, and the on or off state is announced
It only works with an icon
extraQuiz.explanation: Standard controls are already accessible; the title becomes the label. Use 'accessibilityLabel' when the label is just an icon or image.

extraQuiz.question: What does SecureField guarantee?
options: Hides the characters shown on screen; protecting the data is the app's responsibility
extraQuiz.explanation: 'SecureField' only masks the display. For passwords, also use 'textContentType(.password)' for autofill and store credentials in the Keychain.

title: SwiftUI: Animations, Gestures and Presentations
theory: There are two ways to animate in SwiftUI: implicit, '.animation(_:value:)', animates changes to animatable properties whenever the observed 'value' changes, and explicit, 'withAnimation { }', animates everything that depends on the state changes made inside the closure. Opacity, scale, rotation, offset and colors are animatable because they can be numerically interpolated. Curves such as '.easeInOut' and springs such as '.spring' (or '.spring(duration:bounce:)', where bounce 0 removes the overshoot) feel natural. A 'transition' defines how a view enters and leaves the hierarchy, but it only animates when the insertion or removal happens inside an animation; 'matchedGeometryEffect' with '@Namespace' makes the same view appear to move between two layouts. Gestures such as 'TapGesture', 'LongPressGesture', 'DragGesture' and 'MagnifyGesture' are attached with 'gesture' and combined with 'simultaneously(with:)', 'sequenced(before:)' or 'exclusively(before:)'; '@GestureState' holds values that return to their initial state when the gesture ends. For presentations, 'sheet', 'fullScreenCover', 'popover', 'alert' and 'confirmationDialog' are driven by a Bool ('isPresented') or an optional item ('item'), and 'presentationDetents' sets the sheet heights. Inside the presented view, '@Environment(\.dismiss)' closes it. 'onAppear' runs when the view appears, and 'task' runs asynchronous work that is cancelled automatically when the view disappears.
corporateCase: In a booking app, tapping a hotel opens a 'sheet' with half-height 'presentationDetents', and the Confirm button uses 'withAnimation' to switch screens with a smooth transition. A 'confirmationDialog' asks how to cancel the booking, and '.task' loads availability when the screen appears.
gameCase: In a card game, each card uses 'DragGesture' to be dragged and 'matchedGeometryEffect' to fly from the hand to the table. A 'LongPressGesture' shows the card detail and a '.spring' animation adds a bounce when it is released.

quiz.question: What is the difference between '.animation(_:value:)' and 'withAnimation'?
options: The first animates the view's observed changes when 'value' changes; the second animates every change caused by a block of code
quiz.explanation: The implicit form is attached to the view and reacts to a value; the explicit form wraps the state change and affects everything that depends on it.

quiz.question: What does 'matchedGeometryEffect(id:in:)' require to work?
options: Two views with the same id and the same '@Namespace', in different states of the interface
quiz.explanation: The two views share an identifier and namespace, and SwiftUI interpolates position and size between them when the swap happens inside an animation.

quiz.question: 'if show { Text("Hi").transition(.slide) }' and 'show.toggle()' with no animation at all. What happens?
options: The view appears and disappears without animating, because the transition only runs inside an animation
quiz.explanation: Transitions depend on an animation context, such as 'withAnimation { show.toggle() }' or '.animation(_:value:)' on the container.

quiz.question: Which gesture modifier runs two gestures in order, the second only after the first succeeds?
quiz.explanation: 'LongPressGesture().sequenced(before: DragGesture())' requires the long press before the drag, a pattern used to reorder items.

quiz.question: How do you make a sheet occupy half the screen and be expandable?
quiz.explanation: 'presentationDetents' defines the allowed heights. The modifier goes on the presented content view inside the sheet.

quiz.question: How can a view presented by 'sheet' close itself?
options: It cannot, only the parent closes it
quiz.explanation: The environment's 'dismiss' action closes the current presentation (sheet, pushed screen and so on), without passing a Binding down.

quiz.question: What is the advantage of '.task { }' over '.onAppear { Task { } }'?
options: The asynchronous work is cancelled automatically when the view disappears
It always runs on another thread
quiz.explanation: 'task' is tied to the view's lifecycle: it accepts 'await' directly and the task is cancelled on exit. 'task(id:)' restarts when the id changes.

quiz.question: What does '.spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0)' produce?
options: A smooth spring movement with no oscillation past the target
An animation with a lot of bounce
quiz.explanation: 'bounce' controls the overshoot: 0 never exceeds the final value, while higher values oscillate more.

extraQuiz.question: When should you choose 'confirmationDialog' over 'alert'?
options: For the user to choose among several related actions, such as Save, Discard or Cancel
extraQuiz.explanation: 'alert' informs or asks for a short confirmation; 'confirmationDialog' presents a set of action choices to the user.

extraQuiz.question: How does 'fullScreenCover' differ from 'sheet'?
options: It covers the whole interface and is not dismissed by swiping; you must close it from code
extraQuiz.explanation: 'fullScreenCover' is used for immersive flows (onboarding, camera) that the app controls with a button and 'dismiss'.

extraQuiz.question: Which gesture detects pinch-to-zoom on iOS 17 and later?
options: MagnifyGesture, whose value carries the 'magnification' property
extraQuiz.explanation: 'MagnifyGesture' replaces the older 'MagnificationGesture' and exposes 'value.magnification' to adjust the scale.

extraQuiz.question: What happens to a '@GestureState' when the gesture ends?
options: It automatically returns to its initial value
extraQuiz.explanation: '@GestureState' is temporary: it resets to the initial value when the gesture ends or is cancelled. For permanent values, store the result in '@State' in 'onEnded'.

extraQuiz.question: How does a 'popover' behave by default on an iPhone (compact width)?
options: It adapts to a sheet; this can be changed with 'presentationCompactAdaptation'
It always floats as a bubble
extraQuiz.explanation: In compact widths the popover is adapted. 'presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover)' asks to keep it as a bubble.

extraQuiz.question: What is the advantage of 'sheet(item:)' over 'sheet(isPresented:)'?
options: It presents using an optional Identifiable item and uses the value to build the content, returning to nil on dismissal
It removes the need for dismiss
extraQuiz.explanation: With 'item', the content receives the selected value directly and the Binding returns to nil on dismissal, avoiding inconsistent states.
